searchText: I did some benchmarking of the point eval precompile, based on go-ethereum (which is based on go-kzg). Results are here: https://github.com/ethereum/benchmarking/blob/master/shanghai/README.md -- based on that, I'd recommend pricing it at 100K (bump by 2x). The actual test vectors used can be found on this branch: https://github.com/holiman/go-ethereum/commits/eip-4844 So I've found a more up to date prysm impl here: https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/commits/eip4844 Is there a geth/erigon implementation that includes withdrawals fields in the APIs? geth: https://github.com/mdehoog/go-ethereum (eip-4844 branch) When testing against this, I got errors saying `V2` endpoints don't exist. It does look like withdrawals support is included there, so maybe support is included on `V1` endpoints? which endpoints? the `bls_to_execution_changes` one for example is a `v1` endpoint endpoints related to payloads (getPayload, newPayload ) AFAIK, the endpoints haven't been implemented in any EL client yet. <@390327547038007297> is working on adding them to geth. Yup, let me see if I can get to this today. <@607055410104500244> if you dm me your github ID I can tag you on any PRs? thanks! can do **4844 Implementers' Call tomorrow 15:30 UTC** Agenda: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/679 Hi <@415109946682769408> have we had a chance to re-build spec tests with https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3127 ? Would love for all of us to to be passing 4844 spec tests before any testnet Thanks for doing this. Yeah it makes sense to me that it should be 100K for the average worse case. Are the other precompiles priced using a similarly using worse case benchmarks? Yes, we have tried to find the worst cases, and price based off of that. However, the go-kzg might be not the final form, or fully optimized yet (?). Its performance characteristic is similar to the final form c-kzg. They both use the same algo pairing algo so I imagine the worst expensive fuzz corpuses will have identical benchmarks. ~~I tried running the test cases directly on go-kzg and I’m getting sporadic results, did this happen for you?~~ Linter added an implicit conversion Ie the worse case changes depending on the benchmark run. Asking because its not 100% intuitive to me that the failure case takes longer than the correct case, I would have expected the failure cases to be faster due to not passing some precondition checks or around the same Here is the branch I'm using to benchmark the failure cases on go-kzg for critique: https://github.com/kevaundray/go-kzg/blob/kw/benchmark-gas-cost/eth/eth_test.go#L26 So the benchmark decodes the hex string into bytes, calls the precompile and benchmarks how long it takes to execute the pointEval function. Let me know if theres a discrepancy between those benchmarks and the ones that produced the increase in memory usage

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content: I did some benchmarking of the point eval precompile, based on go-ethereum (which is based on go-kzg). Results are here: https://github.com/ethereum/benchmarking/blob/master/shanghai/README.md  -- based on that, I'd recommend pricing it at 100K (bump by 2x).

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content: The actual test vectors used can be found on this branch: https://github.com/holiman/go-ethereum/commits/eip-4844

excerpts.author: realbigsean
excerpts.content:
So I've found a more up to date prysm impl here: https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/commits/eip4844

Is there a geth/erigon implementation that includes withdrawals fields in the APIs?

excerpts.author: realbigsean
excerpts.content: When testing against this, I got errors saying `V2` endpoints don't exist. It does look like withdrawals support is included there, so maybe support is included on `V1`  endpoints?

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: which endpoints? the `bls_to_execution_changes` one for example is a `v1` endpoint

excerpts.author: inphi
excerpts.content: AFAIK, the endpoints haven't been implemented in any EL client yet. <@390327547038007297> is working on adding them to geth.

excerpts.author: roberto.bayardo
excerpts.content: Yup, let me see if I can get to this today. <@607055410104500244> if you dm me your github ID I can tag you on any PRs?

Are the other precompiles priced using a similarly using worse case benchmarks?

excerpts.content:
Yes, we have tried to find the worst cases, and price based off of that. 

However, the go-kzg might be not the final form, or fully optimized yet (?).

excerpts.author: inphi
